race_overlay.weather: August in Gorham, New Hampshire — Mid-August at the Auto Road base starts mild (60-75F) but conditions deteriorate rapidly with altitude. Mt. Washington holds the record for the highest wind gust directly measured at the Earth's surface: 231 mph. The summit's yearly average temperature is 33.9F — no temperature above 72F has ever been recorded there. Even on a calm August race day, summit conditions can include fog, rain, high winds, and temperatures 20-30 degrees colder than the base. The weather observatory on the summit exists specifically because this mountain produces some of the most extreme weather on Earth. Rehearse adaptable layers and race-day kit changes in the final 2 weeks, including rain protection and wet-road braking, and practice stable positioning in crosswinds before Mt. Washington Auto Road Bicycle Hillclimb (MWARBH). Use the organizer's current forecast and safety instructions for final choices.
